newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-GMexico Q4 results seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-GMexico Q4 results seen up.

text.p: Mexico's largest mining company Grupo Mexico SA (GMexico) is expected to report slightly weaker earnings for the year compared with 1995, analysts said, but fourth quarter results are seen stronger on a combination of a slide in the peso and a recovery of world copper prices, analysts said.
Year earnings are expected to come in lower on the peso's strength for most of the year and on ailing copper prices. GMexico's sales are heavily weighted in export dollars.
An average of three analysts forecasted earnings of 3.87 pesos per share for 1996, compared with 6.30 pesos per share in 1995.

"Operating profit declined (for the year), as production volume on average was up slightly and prices were down slightly. The earnings drop gets exaggerated by Mexican inflation accounting," Credit Lyonnais analyst David Bodenberg said.
Mexican accounting calculates for inflation in peso-dollar conversions, Bodenberg said, which exaggerates the peso's real worth in 1996.
Such calculations mar earnings of large exporters with revenues in dollars, such as Grupo Mexico.
In the first nine months of 1996, the company reported net profit of 1.82 billion pesos, with earnings per share of 2.64 pesos.

Lower world copper prices took a bite out of earnings in the first nine months. But in the fourth quarter the situation reversed. In addition to a rebound in copper prices, the company got a boost in the fourth quarter from a weaker peso.
Valores Finamex brokerage analyst Chris Albi said GMexico should report sales of about $300 million for the quarter with an expected $100 million in sales per month.
"Operations look good, pretty solid. The company has been cutting costs," Albi said.

"To the extent that (copper) prices are up it will benefit the company, and on the other hand, we expect greater sales because of their expansion program," BBV-Probursa brokerage analyst Jose Buendia said.
The recently completed Caridad smelter expansion in Sonora state will increase the production of anode copper by at least 100,000 tonnes in 1997, Bodenberg wrote in a recent report.

But despite higher output and improved sales, the company was frustrated in its failed bid to operate the Northeast Railway, a key trade route from the country's main center to ports and U.S. border cities.
Analysts said they expect the company to pursue concessions to operate some of the shorter railways scheduled for auction in the first months of 1997.

Also, the company has yet to buy back 105 million shares owned by U.S.-based ASARCO Inc. A purchase of the almost 23 percent of the company's shares held by Asarco could also be pending, analysts said.
ASARCO has openly stated its desire to offload the holding and GMexico is expected to buy back the shares, but the two are stuck in negotiations over price.
